To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HITRAN and the GEISA H2O line parameters are not accurate enough to derive water vapor abundances in the Venus deep atmosphre.
the water vapor abundance in Venus deep atmosphere has been underestimated due to the use of incorrect water vapor line parameters in previous studies.

there is a significant discrepancy between water vapor mixing ratios derived using the early high- temperature H2O line list by Meadows and Crisps (Meadows, 1996) and the more recently developed BT2 line list of Barber et al. (Barber, 2006).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the water vapor abundance in the Venus lower atmosphere using near-infrared observations.
the study of the composition and structure of the Venus atmosphere.
the determination of the water vapor content of the Venus atmosphere.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the water vapor mixing ratios derived for Venus from the 1.4, 1.7, and 2.3 μm windows are all too low, while the 1.1 μm window is probably too high, and the 1.8 μm window is uncertain due to the lack of data in the 8000–9500 cm− 1 region.

the water vapor mixing ratios derived by previous studies of the Venus deep atmosphere using the HITRAN and/or GEISA lists are likely overestimates of the true value by 20–40% and that the BT2 list should be used instead.
the water abundance in the Venus deep atmospheric is still not known accurately.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Venus atmosphere is not as dry as previously thought and that it may not be as dry as previously measured.

there is a need for a new Venus H2O line list that is based on the latest high-temperature calculations and includes all of the lines in the Venus deep atmospheres that are needed for accurate modeling of the H2 O abundance in the 1.1 to 2.0 μm region.
the Venus water vapor abundance derived from the 1.38 and 1.18 microns windows is 27 ± 4 ppm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the H2O line list used to derive the Venus deep atmosphere water abundance is very important and that there are significant differences in water abundances that can result from different line lists.
the H2O mixing ratios derived in previous Venus deep atmosphere studies are probably too high.
it is essential to use an accurate and complete line list when determining water abundances at Venus, particularly in the deep atmosphere.
